libraries.paragraph: The MAX14521E is a quad high-voltage EL lamp driver with I²C interface made by Maxim Integrated. It is designed to drive up to four electroluminescent (EL) lamps, typically used as backlighting in display applications such as mobile phones, laptops and other portable devices. The IC can drive EL lamps up to 150V, with a maximum current of 20mA per channel, allowing for high brightness and efficient operation. It also includes an I²C interface for easy control and integration into the system. Additionally, the IC includes several safety features, such as over-voltage and over-current protection, to ensure safe and reliable operation. The IC is available in a small, 20-pin TQFN package and it is operated from a single 2.5V to 5.5V supply voltage.

libraries.name: FC0003390327

It is designed to be used in a wide range of IoT and M2M applications, such as smart metering, remote control, tracking, and more. The EG25-G supports both LTE FDD and LTE TDD bands and it is compliant with 3GPP Release 14. It also supports HSPA+/UMTS and GSM/GPRS networks, which means that it can provide fallback options in case of LTE network unavailability. Additionally, it supports GPS/GLONASS/Beidou positioning and it has embedded multi-constellation GNSS receiver, which enables easy and precise positioning. The module is available in a compact LCC package, measuring only 22.5mm x 30mm x 2.5mm and it is designed to operate in extreme temperature conditions. The module also supports various features such as, USB 2.0, UART, and I2C interfaces, embedded TCP/IP stack, and more.

It is a low-power, low-cost device designed for use in a wide range of electronic applications that require accurate timekeeping. The RV-8263 features a built-in oscillator, which provides a highly accurate timebase, and a backup battery input that allows it to continue to keep accurate time even when the main power supply is disrupted. The device provides year, month, date, hours, minutes, and seconds information, and supports both 12-hour and 24-hour time formats. It also has a number of programmable alarm and timer functions, and can generate square wave output signals for use with external circuits.

Management of the file system via Admin mimicking Windows File Explorer with Drag&Drop. (3) Performance metrics to monitor IoT server application and extensions beyond the simple logging of Serial Monitor.  Watch variables and logging supports runtime disabling and remote viewing of messages from the browser Admin. (4) Customizable, Windows style Task Manager type histogram that can also be used for IoT application custom variables.  (5) Custom high-performance API using WebSockets for responsive and high-rate communications between browser clients and ESP8266 IoT server. Declarative DSL: file-scope blocks like ISimpleButton("btn1") { WHEN_PRESSED { ... } } — no boilerplate. Compact binary protocol about 5x smaller than JSON. libraries.name: Itty Bitty
libraries.author: Tom Biuso <tjbtech@yahoo.com>
libraries.sentence:
With the fastest possible Arduino-compatible GPIO and register manipulation...
It's the biggest of hits when you need to bang bits!
libraries.paragraph:
Getting tired of mindlessly staring down your wristwatch in an open-mouthed gape, awaiting a digitalRead's return? Do you long for a super-simple way to set or flip your bits? Has repeatedly ALT-TABing to the ATmega datasheets to look up register descriptions worn you down to the last raw nerve?

Then, golly gee, this lib is here to allay your despair!

In fact, it was made for you - whether an Arduino n00b, hopelessly ignorant to the time their programs waste on the simplest IO tasks, or an AVR guru and uber-smart embedded god, who never even gave a thought to seeking an easier way to bang bits. Most of all, however, this library is for the wretched, cursed signals stuck in the maze of your Arduino's buffers. For it is they who fly through pin lines at the speed of light only to quietly suffer the most indignant fate at the hands of non-performant source code: WAITING.

So set those bits free with a little help from your friends - a plenitude of easy-to-use functions, macros, and data structures in this simple, elegant library that will give your code real legs. But, more importantly, it makes coding that much more FUNNER.

libraries.paragraph: jm_crc-ccitt CRC-CCITT Arduino Library computes the CRC-CCITT values of various data. The library includes also <constexpr> definitions to compute CRC values of constants at compile time. CRC-CCITT is a 16-bit CRC. jm_crc-ccitt is based and uses the AVR optimized library <util/crc16.h> and its generic implementation for non-AVR architectures, which is also the CRC algorithm used by the Bridge Arduino Library. To compute online CRC values, you can click the link https://crccalc.com/?method=CRC-16/MCRF4XX. More explanations about MCFF4XX can be found in https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/40232J.pdf and the Application Note 752 https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/AppNotes/00752a.pdf (take care of particular byte/nibble orders).

libraries.name: Keyhole
libraries.author: Jeremy Hill <jezhill@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: A lightweight library for serial-port interaction: send commands and get/set sketch variables via a JSON- and Python-compatible text interface.
libraries.paragraph:
In one line, and usually with less than a microsecond of overhead, keyhole.variable("foo", foo); provides serial-port access to an integer, floating-point or String variable in your sketch. Set its value by sending foo=123
 - the variable() method will return true to let the sketch know when you do this. Query it by sending foo
 . Query all exposed variables at once by sending ?
 , or choose to have them auto-report themselves periodically. Responses are in easy-to-parse JSON format and can be turned into Python dicts with one call to ast.literal_eval(), but there's a plotter-compatibility mode too. For the computer's side of the interaction, a complementary Python module is included in the project repository (or available separately from PyPI with python -m pip install keyhole-comm[serial] ).

libraries.sentence: A library for HD44780 based LCDs.

It has ability to edit some text right on the LCD screen, eg. insert and delete a character, backspace, move cursor in all directions (left, right, up, and down), newline, line home, and line end. It also supports println() method, read character or text right from the LCD screen (no longer need to waste some expensive MCU RAMs to buffering the text currently being edited). So you can edit your text on the screen without messing with complex code. All used I/O pins, except EN pin, are shareable with other hardware. For example if it used with a matrix keypad, then the databus pins (DB4, DB5, DB6, and DB7) can be shared with the keypad column only or the row pins only. Do not share them with mixed any column and row pins together to avoid unexpected behaviour on accessing the LCD while a key is being pressed.

libraries.sentence: Lean dynamic Array, Queue and Stack for embedded C++.
libraries.paragraph: Minimal, allocation-frugal Array<T>/Queue<T>/Stack<T> for microcontrollers. Designed for trivially-copyable element types (primitives, PODs, raw pointers) — enforced at compile time. Non-copyable, header-only, no dependencies. libraries.name: LionDallas
libraries.author: leva <leva.the.lion@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Compact DS18B20 driver over OneWire for the Lion* stack (ESP8266 / ESP32).
libraries.paragraph: Discovers DS18B20 addresses once at startup and keeps them (cures "the second sensor drops off"); reads them non-blocking; caches the last good reading and rides out transient -127/fault values for a tolerance window. Includes the DallasTemperature 4.0.6 power-on-reset / insufficient-power / fault detection. Optional fixed addresses skip the unreliable SearchROM on long wiring (read by MatchROM). DS18B20 family (0x28) only. The consumer defines one global LionLogger Logger. On ESP8266 the reads run in a LionTask LionCriticalTask (pump LionTask::Loop() from loop()); on ESP32 they run in a dedicated LionRtosTask FreeRTOS task (no pump needed). Portions ported from the Arduino Temperature Control Library (c) Miles Burton, MIT.

libraries.name: LionFastLcd
libraries.author: leva <leva.the.lion@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Change-tracked, buffered character-LCD layer over LiquidCrystal_I2C.
libraries.paragraph: Keeps a RAM shadow of the display and pushes only the cells that actually changed, coalescing runs of consecutive cells into a single setCursor() to cut I2C traffic. Implements Arduino Print, so use print()/println() as usual. Supports stacked/overlay screens via Clone()/Activate()/Deactivate() with a z-order. The class is non-copyable and objects are created only through CreateMain()/Clone() (they register in a static list and are meant to live for the program's lifetime); call CreateMain() once before any Clone()/Activate(). The shadow buffer is cols*rows bytes. Depends on LionArray and marcoschwartz/LiquidCrystal_I2C. Optional scrolling of over-long lines is ESP8266-only and OFF by default: build with -DFLCD_LONG_MESSAGES and add leva/LionTask. ESP8266 + AVR.

libraries.name: LionLogger
libraries.author: leva <leva.the.lion@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Small leveled logger for ESP8266 / ESP32.
libraries.paragraph: Logs to Serial and/or the internal filesystem (SPIFFS or LittleFS) with level filtering, dated log files, size/age-based rotation and free-space management. Optional async (FreeRTOS) logging on ESP32 (pulls in LionRtosTask). Non-copyable single-instance logger. ESP8266/ESP32 only — no SD, no AVR.

libraries.name: LionRtosTask
libraries.author: leva <leva.the.lion@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Tiny OOP wrapper over FreeRTOS tasks for ESP32.
libraries.paragraph: Subclass RtosTask, override TaskBody(), and run it as a Standard (loops forever), EveryMs (one step every N ms) or Waiting (one step per TaskNotify()) task pinned to a core. Ships critical-section helpers and RtosSimpleTask for running a lambda once or periodically. Tasks own their OS handles: they are non-copyable, and self-deleting tasks must be heap-allocated. ESP32 only. Depends on LionArray.

libraries.name: LionStreams
libraries.author: leva <leva.the.lion@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Tiny Arduino Stream adapters: a String-backed stream and a chunk-flushing web-server stream.
libraries.paragraph: StringStream is a read/write Stream view over an external String (non-owning — the String must outlive the stream; reset() rewinds the read cursor and clears the String). ServerStream is a write-only Stream that buffers Print output and flushes it in chunks via server.sendContent() on ESP8266WebServer / ESP32 WebServer, so large HTML pages stream out without holding the whole response in RAM (start a chunked/unknown-length response first and call flush() at the end). Both are header-only and non-copyable. For ESPAsyncWebServer use the built-in beginResponseStream() instead.

libraries.name: LionTask
libraries.author: leva <leva.the.lion@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Tiny cooperative (run-to-completion) task scheduler for ESP8266 and AVR.
libraries.paragraph: Pump LionTask::Loop() from loop(); each task runs to completion on the main context (no preemption, no per-task stack). Subclass LionTimerTask / LionShortTimerTask / LionCrudeTimerTask / LionCriticalTask and override TaskInnerBody(), or use LionSimpleTask to run a lambda without subclassing (ESP only). Critical tasks also run during Yield()/Delay(). Tasks register themselves by pointer and are non-copyable: create each once as a global/static or via new. Depends on LionArray. ESP8266 + AVR (on ESP32 use LionRtosTask instead).

libraries.name: LionWifi
libraries.author: leva <leva.the.lion@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: WiFi connection manager with ArduinoOTA, a web filesystem browser and a status page, for ESP8266 and ESP32.
libraries.paragraph: Pumps the WiFi state machine (multi-SSID connect, auto-reconnect, AP rotation, optional router-ping reboot), sets time over NTP, rotates logs, runs ArduinoOTA, and serves a SPIFFS/LittleFS/SD file browser (list/upload/download/tail/delete) plus log views over ESP8266WebServer or (ESP32) ESPAsyncWebServer/WebServer. The consumer defines three globals (the LionLogger `Logger`, the web `server`, and `WifiConnector *_connector`) and selects a filesystem with -D USE_SPIFFS or -D LFS. Single-instance, non-copyable. Depends on LionArray, LionLogger, LionStreams, and LionTask (ESP8266) / LionRtosTask (ESP32). The ESP32 async web path also needs ESPAsyncWebServer + AsyncTCP.

libraries.paragraph: The most important feature is they're purely hardware-based PWM channels, supporting very high PWM frequencies. Therefore, their executions are not blocked by bad-behaving functions or tasks. This important feature is absolutely necessary for mission-critical tasks. These hardware-based PWMs, still work even if other software functions are blocking. Moreover, they are much more precise (certainly depending on clock frequency accuracy) than other software-based PWM using ISR, millis() or micros(). That's necessary if you need to control devices requiring high precision. New efficient setPWM_manual function to facilitate waveform creation using PWM. Supporting MegaCoreX.

libraries.name: megaAVR_Slow_PWM

libraries.paragraph: It now supports 16 ISR-based PWM channels, while consuming only 1 Hardware Timer. PWM channel interval can be very long (ulong microsecs / millisecs). The most important feature is they're ISR-based PWM channels, supporting lower PWM frequencies with suitable accuracy. Their executions are not blocked by bad-behaving functions or tasks. This important feature is absolutely necessary for mission-critical tasks. These ISR-based PWMs, still work even if other software functions are blocking. Moreover, they are much more precise (certainly depending on clock frequency accuracy) than other software-based PWM using millis() or micros(). That's necessary if you need to control devices requiring high precision. Now you can change the PWM settings on-the-fly. Now supporting MegaCoreX.

libraries.name: megaAVR_TimerInterrupt

Moreover, they are much more precise (certainly depending on clock frequency accuracy) than other software timers using millis() or micros(). That is mandatory if you need to measure some data requiring better accuracy. It now supports 16 ISR-based Timers, while consuming only 1 Hardware Timer. Timers interval is very long (ulong millisecs). The most important feature is they are ISR-based Timers. Therefore, their executions are not blocked by bad-behaving functions or tasks. libraries.name: MG811SpaceData

libraries.sentence: The first and only Arduino library where MG811 Gas Sensor combine with Data Science

Concentrations of the primary gases are determined by applying the cathodic reaction correction coefficient over 20-second intervals, along with the effects of temperature and humidity on the a and b parameters of the ppm values. Theoretical CO2, on the other hand, is derived from a polynomial curve created based on the Nernst equation. Additionally, the library supports Python-based data science applications, including 4D ppm concentration graph simulations at 20-second intervals and a 4D ppm slope estimation platform for advanced data analysis.

libraries.sentence: Arduino library for driving up to 768 (49152 ESP32, PICO) LEDs, signals, sound modules or other actuators via one signal line on a model railway
libraries.paragraph:
New in release 3.5.0: support LichtMaschine Pico Zero hardware, multiplexer support multiple LED channels, speed up application startup
  • Excel user interface to configure the LEDs without programming at all improved by the engagement of Pattern Configurator and Program Generator!
  • On the basis of WS2811 / WS2812 devices (RGB LEDs), many different effects can easily be controlled via one wire:
    • Animated lighting effects: animated house, soft blending light signals and crossing lights, traffic lights, flashing vehicle lights, construction site security lights, street lamps, funfair effects, disco, photo flash, ...
    • Sounds: 1 Eu sound modules could generate: station announcements, railroad noises, animal sounds, ...
    • Movements With additional hardware servo or stepper motors could be controlled in the same way.
  • Easy cabling: For a model railway the simple wiring is very important. A single 4-pin ribbon cable can supply all consumers on the layout. With multiple plug strips, the LEDs can be flexibly arranged.
  • Thanks to many examples, no programming knowledge is necessary. Anyone who can operate a text editor is able to adapt these examples to the individual circumstances.
  • Other features: very low cost, configurable animation sequences, high update rate, reading of 80 and more switches, logical operations, automatic and manual operation (light dependent, timed, CAN bus, random)...
  • Hardware: The "extras" directory contains schematics and printed circuit boards for this library.

This project would not have been possible without the fantastic FastLED library. => Thank you zackees & jueff

libraries.name: MySQL_MariaDB_Generic
libraries.author: Dr. Charles Bell <chuck.bell@oracle.com>, Khoi Hoang <khoih.prog@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Connects to MySQL or MariaDB using ESP8266/ESP32, WT32_ETH01 (ESP32 + LAN8720A), nRF52, SAMD21/SAMD51, STM32F/L/H/G/WB/MP1, Teensy, SAM DUE, Mega, RP2040-based boards, Portenta_H7, etc. with W5x00, ENC28J60 Ethernet, Teensy 4.1 NativeEthernet/QNEthernet, WiFiNINA modules/shields or Portenta_H7 WiFi/Ethernet. W5x00 can use Ethernet_Generic library. ENC28J60 can use either EthernetENC or UIPEthernet Library.
libraries.paragraph: You can use this library to connect your Arduino project directly to a MySQL / MariaDB server without using an intermediate computer or a web-based or cloud-based service. Having direct access to a database server means you can store data acquired from your project as well as check values stored in tables on the server. This also means you can setup your own, local MySQL / MariaDB server to store your data further removing the need for Internet connectivity. If that is not an issue, you can still connect to and store data on a MySQL / MariaDB server via your network, Internet, or even in the cloud! Now accepting server hostname, besides IPAddress. Ethernet_Generic library is used as default for W5x00

libraries.name: MyTimer
libraries.author: ApophisXX
libraries.sentence: Functions for non-blocking millis() timer.
libraries.paragraph: Functions to be called within the loop to provide different time dependent actions. Easy to use Serial prints, simple button debounce, effective non code blocking events. Sheer unlimited possibilities.

libraries.name: n2cmu
libraries.author: nthnn
libraries.sentence: Feedforward Neural Network Coprocessing Microcontroller Unit (CPC via UART) for STM32F103C8T6 Bluepill Development Board written purely in TinyGo.
libraries.paragraph: N2CMU is a project aimed at implementing a neural network coprocessing microcontroller unit (MCU) for STM32F103C8T6 Bluepill development board using the TinyGo (Go programming language for embedded systems). This MCU enables offloading feedforward neural network computations to a dedicated hardware unit, allowing for efficient and low-power feedforward neural network training and inference on small hardware embedded systems.

libraries.name: N64Controller
libraries.author: Andrew Brown, Peter Den Hartog, Kai Lüke, Daniel Schaal
libraries.sentence: Arduino library to connect a Nintendo 64 controller (N64 controller).

libraries.name: N64Controller-ESP32
libraries.author: Andrew Brown, Peter Den Hartog, Kai Lüke, Daniel Schaal, Haskell
libraries.sentence: Read a Nintendo 64 controller from an ESP32 (Arduino).
libraries.paragraph: ESP32 port of the pothos/arduino-n64-controller-library. Same public API as the AVR original, so existing sketches compile unchanged. Uses cycle-accurate GPIO bit-banging via the Xtensa CCOUNT cycle counter and ESP32 open-drain GPIO mode; no special peripheral driver required.

libraries.name: N64Pad
libraries.author: SukkoPera <software@sukkology.net>
libraries.sentence: Interface with Nintendo 64/GameCube controllers
libraries.paragraph: Only tested with official Nintendo controllers

libraries.name: NaiPot
libraries.author: Artem Nikitin
libraries.sentence: A simple library for working with potentiometers.
libraries.paragraph: Provides easy reading and mapping of potentiometer values with simple interface.

libraries.name: Namino_Industrial_Boards
libraries.author: Namino Team <info@namino.cc>
libraries.sentence: Namino industrial board
libraries.paragraph: Control Universal ±25 V 8-Input High Speed AFE industrial interface 24/16-bit ADC

libraries.name: NanitLib
libraries.author: NanitRobot, Sam4uk
libraries.sentence: A library for Nanit
libraries.paragraph: "Nanit" Robot Education Kit is a robotics constructor that replaces 100 toys, by different assembly options. It has three training programs for children of different ages: for children 5-7 years old - learning the basics of robotics and electronics, learning about the world of robots for children 8-10 years old - robot and games programming using Scratch language, children aged ten and over assemble a prototype of a SMART HOME on Arduino, program in C language.

libraries.name: Nano_Every_WS2812B
libraries.author: Clemens at Elektor
libraries.sentence: ATmega4809 core-independent driver for WS2812B addressable RGB LEDs.
libraries.paragraph: No bit-banging, the communication protocol is handled by hardware peripherals, saving lots of CPU cycles.

libraries.name: Nano33BLESensor
libraries.author: Dale Giancono <d.giancono@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: An Arduino library for the Nano 33 BLE Sense that leverages Mbed OS to automatically place sensor measurements in a ring buffer that can be integrated into programs in a simple manner.
libraries.paragraph: Nano33BLESensor leverages Mbed OS and ring buffers to allow the softening of time constraints in regard to the reading sensor measurements. It also allows simple initialisation of the on board sensors, and provides a simple interface for the getting of sensor data.

libraries.name: NanoBLEFlashPrefs
libraries.author: Dirk Froehling <dirk.froehling@w-hs.de>
libraries.sentence: Substitute for the missing EEPROM storage on Arduino Nano 33 BLE and BLE Sense.
libraries.paragraph: This library allows saving parameters and settings between program restarts and even reflashing on Arduino Nano 33 BLE and BLE Sense. Please note: Starting with version 1.1 of the library, all functions are synchronized. Therefore you should remove waiting loops with calls to operationCompleted() in your existing code.

libraries.name: NanoConnectHcSr04
libraries.author: Alan Yorinks
libraries.sentence: HC-SR04 support for the Arduino Nano RP2040 Connect.
libraries.paragraph: Monitor HC-SR04 type distance sensors on the Arduino Nano RP2040 Connect using an RP2040 PIO processor.

libraries.name: nanoFORTH
libraries.author: chochain <chochain@yahoo.com>
libraries.sentence: A simple and useful Forth for Nano.
libraries.paragraph: Forth in .ino that can be loaded into Nano/UNO. You can interact with it via Serial Monitor or Bluetooth to control pins. Your "app" can be saved into EEROM for autorun on reboot. Interrupt and multi-tasking are also supported.

libraries.name: NanoPlayBoard
libraries.author: Antonio Morales and José Juan Sánchez
libraries.sentence: Enables easy access to the sensors and actuators of the Arduino NanoPlayBoard.
libraries.paragraph: NanoPlayBoard is an educational shield for Arduino Nano, which may be an excellent educational resource for those students who want to learn basic electronic and hardware programming.

libraries.name: NanoProtoShield
libraries.author: Zach English
libraries.sentence: Arduino library to interact with the NanoProtoShield hardware.
libraries.paragraph: This library makes all the accessories of the NanoProtoShield accessable via simple class interactions. Used for educational purposes, this reduces the required learning curve before a student can start doing "fun things" with their board.

libraries.name: Navigador
libraries.author: nthnn
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for dual DC motor navigation.

libraries.name: Naviguider_Compass_I2C
libraries.author: Marine Applied Research & Exploration (Isaac Assegai)
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for Naviguider I2C Compass.
libraries.paragraph: Arduino library for Naviguider I2C Compass enables easy communication with a NaviGuider Compass

libraries.name: NB_Generic
libraries.author: Arduino, Khoi Hoang <khoih.prog@gmail.com>, Miguel Wisintainer <tcpipchip@hotmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Enables NB-IoT/LTE-M/CAT M1 network connection using the Generic NB-IoT modules (u-blox SARA R4, etc.) and boards
libraries.paragraph: Use this library to send and receive SMS using Generic NB-IoT/GPRS modules, such as u-blox SARA-R4xx module.This library also allows you to connect to internet Web Clients through the NB-IoT/LTE-M/CAT M1 networks. Supporting ESP32 (including ESP32-S2, ESP32-C3), ESP8266, Teensy, SAM DUE, SAMD21, SAMD51, STM32F/L/H/G/WB/MP1, nRF52, RP2040-based boards, etc.

libraries.name: nb-twi-cmd
libraries.author: Gustavo Casanova <gustavo.casanova@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: NB TWI command set.
libraries.paragraph: Declares the NB communication protocol over TWI (I2C).

libraries.name: NBitArray
libraries.author: Narwhalsss360
libraries.sentence: Array of bits to save memory instead of using 8-bit boolean values.
libraries.paragraph: Array of bytes container that gets/sets bit values of bytes given bit index.

libraries.name: NbMicro
libraries.author: Gustavo Casanova <gustavo.casanova@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Control devices that implement the NB command set over TWI (I2C).
libraries.paragraph: This library handles the communication protocol with devices that implement the NB command set over a TWI (I2C) bus.

libraries.name: NceCabBus
libraries.author: Alex Shepherd
libraries.sentence: Enables NCE Cab Bus Communication
libraries.paragraph: This library allows you to interface to a NCE Cab Bus and send / receive commands.

libraries.name: NColor
libraries.author: Narwhalsss360
libraries.sentence: NColor Library.
libraries.paragraph: This is the NColor library containing usefuls for manipulating color such as RGB, HSV and xRGB. This also contains RGBLED class to use RGB LEDs.

libraries.name: NDEF_MFRC522
libraries.author: Don Coleman <don.coleman@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: An Arduino library for NFC Data Exchange Format (NDEF).
libraries.paragraph: Read and write NDEF messages to NFC tags and peers. Supports the MFRC522 reader. This library depends on the MFRC522 library https://github.com/miguelbalboa/rfid.

libraries.name: NDefs
libraries.author: Narwhalsss360
libraries.sentence: NDefs library, dependency.
libraries.paragraph: This library is used by other Narwhalsss Libraries.

libraries.name: NDNOverUDP
libraries.author: Antonio Cardace <antonio@cardace.it>, Davide Aguiari <gorghino@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: A simpler and lighter NDN protocol for local IoT contexts.
libraries.paragraph: Named Data Networking (NDN) is a promising paradigm for the future Internet architecture which opens up new possibilities for the data exchange among routers. In order to learn NDN principles, a simpler NDN protocol has been developed in a mobile environment. The library currently works over Ethernet.

libraries.name: NE555
libraries.author: Gfy63 <mrgoofy@gmx.net>
libraries.sentence: Simulation of the function from a NE555 timer chip. ;)
libraries.paragraph: Create puls/flash or delay. On state change a callback function is fired. Delay fires callback only ones.

libraries.name: NecDecoder
libraries.author: AlexGyver <alex@alexgyver.ru>
libraries.sentence: Light library for IR receiver with NEC protocol
libraries.paragraph: Light library for IR receiver with NEC protocol

libraries.name: NECK
libraries.author: Nilson Lazarin
libraries.sentence: Embodied cognition communication kit for agent-based control of physical bodies
libraries.paragraph: NECK (ageNt Embodied Cognition Kit) is a lightweight communication library that enables cognitive agents to interact with physical bodies through expressive bodily responses, supporting embodied cognition in embedded and robotic systems.

libraries.name: Neo7Segment
libraries.author: UnexpectedMaker
libraries.sentence: A library to display numbers and letters on Neo7Segment displays.
libraries.paragraph: Can also be used with neopixel type strips constructed like a 7 segment display. The library can be used to both display and animate the visuals in many different ways.

libraries.name: NeoBufferedPrint
libraries.author: SlashDevin
libraries.sentence: Intermediate printing class for reducing the number of writes.
libraries.paragraph: Dramatically improves performance on IoT-type devices.

libraries.name: NeoGPS
libraries.author: SlashDevin
libraries.sentence: NMEA and ublox GPS parser, configurable to use as few as 10 bytes of RAM
libraries.paragraph: Faster and smaller than all other GPS parsers

libraries.name: NeoGPS-GarminClock
libraries.author: SlashDevin, Patrick Scruggs
libraries.sentence: NeoGPS fork configured for Garmin 18x LVC clock projects.
libraries.paragraph: Fork of NeoGPS configured for Garmin GPS 18x LVC PGRMF leap-second parsing, interrupt-driven NMEA handling, DOP fields, and compatibility with pjscruggs/Timezone64.

libraries.name: NeoHome
libraries.author: MAHESHKUMAR M <maheshkumarm001234@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Control the devices from any where from the NeoHome APp.
libraries.paragraph: Provides a Iot Controls on the remotely using the NeoHome App and the app use the virtual pin for separate the each component.

libraries.name: NeoHWSerial
libraries.author: Georg Icking-Konert
libraries.sentence: NeoHWSerial for AVR
libraries.paragraph: Adaptation of NeoHWSerial by SlashDevin for AVR

libraries.name: NeoNextion
libraries.author: Dan Nixon
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for controlling Nextion displays
libraries.paragraph: Arduino library for controlling Nextion displays

libraries.name: NeonPostgresOverHTTP
libraries.author: Peter Bendel <bodobolero @ gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Store sensor data in PostgreSQL. SQL over HTTP for Arduino
libraries.paragraph: Submit SQL to your PostgreSQL database using HTTP requests with Json payloads. Supports PostgeSQL servers configured with Neon proxy.

libraries.name: NeoPatterns
libraries.author: Armin Joachimsmeyer
libraries.sentence: Patterns for NeoPixel strips and matrixes including the patterns of the NeoPattern example by Adafruit.
libraries.paragraph: Patterns not from Adafruit are: SCANNER, STRIPES, FLASH, TWINKLE, DELAY, PROCESS_SELECTIVE, FADE_SELECTIVE. The original SCANNER pattern is extended and includes the CYLON as well as the ROCKET or FALLING_STAR pattern. The more versatile STRIPES pattern replaces the old THEATER_CHASE one. NeoPixel-Matrix pattern are: MOVING_PICTURE, MOVE, TICKER, FIRE, SNOW, SNAKE.

libraries.name: NeoPixel Painter
libraries.author: DedeHai
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for easy creation of LED strip animations, based on the NeoPixel library.
libraries.paragraph: It uses HSV colors, supports fade-in and fade-out of pixels, fading colors and fading color saturation. See examples for some inspiration.

libraries.name: NeoPixel-Animation-lib
libraries.author: Jan Reiner <jan.reiner@icloud.com>, DracoRex462
libraries.sentence: LED animation library for ESP32 with NeoPixel and FreeRTOS support.
libraries.paragraph: Provides multiple LED animation modes using Adafruit NeoPixel and FreeRTOS tasks for ESP32 boards. Ideal for IoT status indicators and signal lighting.

libraries.name: NeoPixelBus by Makuna
libraries.author: Michael C. Miller (makuna@live.com)
libraries.sentence: A library that makes controlling NeoPixels (WS2812x and many others) and DotStars (SK6812 and many others) easy.
libraries.paragraph: Supports most Arduino platforms, including async hardware support for Esp8266, Esp32, RP2040, and Nrf52 (Nano 33 BLE).  Support for RGBW pixels and 7 Segment LED direct driven.  Includes separate RgbColor, RgbwColor, Rgb16Color, Rgb48Color, HslColor, and HsbColor objects.  Includes an animator class that helps create asyncronous animations.  Supports Matrix layout of pixels.  Includes Gamma corretion object.  For all platforms; there are two methods of sending DotStar data, hardware SPI and software SPI.

libraries.name: NeopixelCommander
libraries.author: Thomas Geissl
libraries.sentence: Control NeoPixels over WebSocket using ESP32 or ESP32-S2.
libraries.paragraph: NeopixelCommander provides a simple, asynchronous WebSocket interface for controlling NeoPixel (WS2812) LEDs via network messages. Built on ESPAsyncWebServer and Adafruit NeoPixel, it enables real-time RGB updates from browsers or network clients.

libraries.name: NeoPixelConnect
libraries.author: Alan Yorinks
libraries.sentence: An experimental NeoPixel Library for the Arduino Nano RP2040 Connect.
libraries.paragraph: This library is based upon the examples provided in the Raspberry Pi Pico C-SDK.

libraries.name: Neosegment
libraries.author: Maks Surguy <maks@neosegment.com>
libraries.sentence: Simple control of Neosegment Displays
libraries.paragraph: Provides an interface for Neosegment LED displays

libraries.name: NeoStreaming
libraries.author: Nerdsiah
libraries.sentence: A fully fuctional, Zero-Heap C++ Streaming Library for Embedded Systems.
libraries.paragraph: Implements a Zero-Heap Proxy Pattern for C++ style stream manipulation (<<, setw, setprecision, fixed, hexfloat, etc.) without the memory fragmentation of the Arduino String class.

libraries.name: NeoSWSerial
libraries.author: SlashDevin
libraries.sentence: An efficient replacement for SoftwareSerial at baud rates 9600, 19200 and 38400.
libraries.paragraph: Simultaneous RX & TX, does not require additional TIMERs, interrupts not disabled during RX

libraries.name: Neotimer
libraries.author: Jose Rullan <jerullan@yahoo.com>
libraries.sentence: "A powerful non-blocking timer"
libraries.paragraph: New debounce function. Non-blocking timer with extended functionality for versatility in a variety of timing scenarios. start,stop,restart,done,waiting and repeat functionality.

libraries.name: NESControllerInterface
libraries.author: Harry's Lab <dev@harryslab.net>
libraries.sentence: An interface for the NES controller
libraries.paragraph: A simple interface for the NES controller, allowing for the 8 buttons of the NES controller to be read by a microcontroller.

libraries.name: NesGamepad
libraries.author: Yaroslav Metelev
libraries.sentence: Yet another library to read buttons from NES (aka Famicom, aka Dendy) gamepad.
libraries.paragraph: This library allows to connect gamepad from NES to Arduino and read buttons from it. No gamepad hardware modification needed.

libraries.name: NesRob
libraries.author: Zachary J. Fields
libraries.sentence: Manipulates the Nintendo R.O.B. (Robotic Operating Buddy).
libraries.paragraph: This library attaches to a specified digital output GPIO, and generates the signals required to control R.O.B.

libraries.name: NessoLink
libraries.author: Ugur Sayar <ugursayar@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Versioned binary control-link protocol for the Nesso N1 robot controller.
libraries.paragraph: RemoteFrame v1/v2 codec (motors, up to two aux sticks, a 16-button bitfield, CRC-8 checked) plus WiFi UDP, TCP, BLE and LoRa (RadioLib) transports. The codec is header-only and dependency-free, so it runs on both the transmitter and the robot receiver on any board; each transport is compile-guarded, so codec-only users pull in no heavy dependencies.

libraries.name: NetApiHelpers
libraries.author: Juraj Andrassy
libraries.sentence: Arduino Networking API helper classes and tests
libraries.paragraph: Useful classes and tests for Arduino Networking API implementations

libraries.name: NetEEPROM
libraries.author: Greg Tan <greg@gregtan.com>
libraries.sentence: A library that stores and retrieves network configuration from EEPROM.
libraries.paragraph: This allows the a network configuration to be stored once, efectively tying network information to the hardware. Once set up, multiple sketches running on the same hardware will retrieve the same network information and the same sketch running on multiple boards will receive a different network configuration for each board.

libraries.name: NETSGPClient
libraries.author: Aaron Christophel, Moritz Wirger
libraries.sentence: Interface for MicroInverters speaking the so-called NETSGP protocol.
libraries.paragraph: An LC12S 2.4GHz RF module is needed for this library

libraries.name: NetWizard
libraries.author: Ayush Sharma
libraries.sentence: An easy-to-use yet powerful WiFi manager and captive portal library for wireless microcontrollers.
libraries.paragraph: Avoid the hassle of hard-coding WiFi credentials and let NetWizard take care of everything for your device!

libraries.name: NetworkManager
libraries.author: Péter Soós <https://github.com/soosp>
libraries.sentence: Priority-based network connection manager with automatic fallback.
libraries.paragraph: Supports WiFi and Ethernet on ESP32, ESP8266 and AVR. Manages multiple network adapters with priority-based fallback, NTP configuration and thread-safe operation.

libraries.name: NetworkMonitor
libraries.author: Tony Bringardner<tony.bringardner@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: A library to provide remote console functions to a MCU through UDP
libraries.paragraph: The NetworkMonitor tool provides an interface similar to the Arduino SerialMonitor but allows you to monitor and control your MCUs without the USB requirement.

libraries.name: NetworkProfile
libraries.author: Péter Soós
libraries.sentence: Thread-safe network interface configuration profiles for ESP32, ESP8266 and AVR.
libraries.paragraph: Provides WiFiProfile and EthProfile classes for managing network configuration (DHCP/static IP, DNS, NTP, hostname, MAC address) with thread-safe access, persistent storage via Preferences, and JSON serialisation. Supports interface priority for fallback scenarios (e.g. ETH → WiFi). Depends on the Host library.

libraries.name: NeuButton
libraries.author: Ulywae <ulywae@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Ultra-low RAM, deterministic multi-button engine using bitmasking.
libraries.paragraph: NeuButton v2 introduces a zero-cost template architecture with auto-adaptive masking (8/16/32-bit), drastically reducing RAM usage by up to 60%.

libraries.name: NeuDB
libraries.author: Ulywae <ulywae@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Ultra-lean, transactional Twin-Engine LSM-Tree storage engine with power-fail resilient lifecycle protection for ESP32.
libraries.paragraph: Asynchronous Log-Structured Merge-tree storage engine tailored for write-heavy embedded logging and circular telemetry tracking. Utilizing an isolated FreeRTOS background compaction scheduler on CPU Core 1, real-time adaptive dynamic boundary monitors, integrated hardware-backed Bloom Filters, and binary index lookaheads, it minimizes flash write amplification and slashes read latencies down to microseconds. Features atomic Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) packed with hardware CRC32 for bulletproof cold crash recovery against sudden power sabotage.

libraries.name: NeuEEPROM
libraries.author: Ulywae <ulywae@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Lightweight and safe EEPROM system for ESP32/ESP8266
libraries.paragraph: Slot-based EEPROM with alignment, CRC, and safe commit system

libraries.name: NeuFrame
libraries.author: Ulywae <ulywae@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: A lightweight, secure, and non-blocking binary framing protocol.
libraries.paragraph: NeuFrame is designed for reliable communication between microcontrollers (Arduino, ESP32, STM32). It features a template-based memory management, CRC16 Modbus integrity check, optional XOR encryption, and a high-precision RS485 frame timer. Perfect for LED controllers (DMX/RS485) and industrial sensor data.

libraries.name: NeuKV
libraries.author: Ulywae (@neufa) <ulywae@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: A lightweight, fast, and powerful NVS wrapper for ESP32 without String overhead.
libraries.paragraph: NeuKV is designed for high-performance ESP32 applications. It uses C++ templates to store any trivially copyable data (like structs, ints, and floats) directly as binary blobs, ensuring zero dynamic memory allocation and no memory fragmentation.

libraries.name: NeumannCorrector
libraries.author: Rob Tillaart <rob.tillaart@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for a NeumannCorrector. (randomizing streams of bits).

libraries.name: NeuNVS
libraries.author: Ulywae <ulywae@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Ultra-fast and secure NVS library for ESP32 with Intelligent Hardware Protection.
libraries.paragraph: NeuNVS is an ID-based storage engine featuring CRC16 integrity, smart auto-commit, and exclusive Thermal Lockdown mode. It includes active wear-leveling (Migration) to protect Flash memory from burn-out and abuse.

libraries.name: NeuraiDepinMsg
libraries.author: Asimov
libraries.sentence: Build, encrypt and sign DePIN messages for Neurai.
libraries.paragraph: A library to create Core-compatible DePIN messages on ESP32. Requires uNeurai library.

libraries.name: NeuralNetwork
libraries.author: George Chousos
libraries.sentence: Simple Neural-Network Library.
libraries.paragraph: ❤ Easy to use, enhanced with user-preference-optimizations and support for: MLP, RNN, GRU, LSTM architectures + FS, SD, PROGMEM, EEPROM, FRAM storage-medias + custom functions and ESP32 DSP-accelerated functionalities.

libraries.name: NeuroMaster
libraries.author: BrainCoTech<yongle.work@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: A library that allows Arduino Uno to interface with NeuroMaster BrainAI Device.
libraries.paragraph: Tested with Uno ATmega328

libraries.name: Neurona
libraries.author: Caio Benatti Moretti
libraries.sentence: Artificial Neural Network architectures for Arduino
libraries.paragraph: This library allows an Arduino board to feed artificial neural network structures, in order to perform tasks such as pattern recognition, non-linear regression and time-series prediction from the available architectures. Click at More info to download the training algorithm of the respective architecture and paste in code the configuration obtained as output.

libraries.name: NeuStorage
libraries.author: Ulywae (@neufa) <ulywae@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: A lightweight, fast, and powerful NVS wrapper for ESP32 without String overhead.
libraries.paragraph: NeuStorage is designed for high-performance ESP32 applications. It uses C++ templates to store any trivially copyable data (like structs, ints, and floats) directly as binary blobs, ensuring zero dynamic memory allocation and no memory fragmentation.

libraries.name: NeuWiFi
libraries.author: Ulywae <ulywae@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: A high-performance native WiFi library for ESP32.
libraries.paragraph: NeuWiFi is built directly on top of ESP-IDF, providing a cleaner and more efficient alternative to the standard Arduino WiFi library. It supports Station, Access Point, and Hybrid modes with a modular architecture.

libraries.name: NEvents
libraries.author: Narwhalsss360
libraries.sentence: NEvents library for adding event handling.
libraries.paragraph: NEvents: This library is used by other libraries that use event handling, see example and info for usage.

libraries.name: NewEncoder
libraries.author: Alex Casal <alexandrocb2013@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: A library that makes coding an rotary encoder a breeze with useful functions
libraries.paragraph: This library do not use interrupt pins so it can be easily utilized by any board. Just make sure to call as frecuently as you can the function Encoder.Update()

libraries.name: Newhaven_CharacterOLED_SPI
libraries.author: BlairBlaidd
libraries.sentence: SPI implementation of Newhaven display DZW series OLED displays.
libraries.paragraph: Implementation of SPI communication on Newhaven DZW series of OLED character displays.  These are amazingly bright and readable displays, but come with parallel interface by default. These displays are able to accept SPI input with a few jumper changes.

libraries.name: NewPID
libraries.author: X-croot <Can Ünüvar>
libraries.sentence: Advanced yet easy Arduino PID controller with anti-windup, derivative filtering, feedforward, bumpless transfer, gain scheduling and built-in Ziegler-Nichols relay and step-response auto-tuning.
libraries.paragraph: AutoPID is a powerful, portable and fully featured PID control library for Arduino, ESP32, ESP8266, STM32 and AVR boards. It supports automatic millis() timing or user supplied dt, output limits, integral anti-windup, derivative-on-measurement with low-pass filtering, feedforward, setpoint ramping, deadband, gain scheduling, bumpless manual/automatic transfer and automatic gain tuning via Ziegler-Nichols relay and open-loop step-response methods. Ideal for temperature control, motor speed, self-balancing robots, drones, line followers, quadcopters and process control.

libraries.name: NewPing
libraries.author: Tim Eckel <eckel.tim@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: NewPing allows interfacing with ultrasonic sensors simple, fast & powerful.
libraries.paragraph: Initially, I was not happy with how poorly ultrasonic sensors performed. I soon realized the problem was not the sensor, it was the available ping and ultrasonic libraries causing the problem. The NewPing library totally fixes these problems, adds many new features, and breathes new life into these very affordable distance sensors.

libraries.name: NewServo
libraries.author: GhassanYusuf
libraries.sentence: An easy-to-use servo motor library for Arduino.
libraries.paragraph: The NewServo Library provides a simple and easy-to-use API for controlling servo motors with Arduino boards.

libraries.name: Newt_Display
libraries.author: Phambili
libraries.sentence: A library to drive the Newt Smart Display.
libraries.paragraph: The Newt is an open-source, low-power, internet connected device. Check out https://github.com/Phambili-Tech/Newt_Display for additional info.

libraries.name: Nexgen_Rover
libraries.author: Peter Januarius
libraries.sentence: The Nexgen_Rover code library contains code to control the Nexgen Rover including a number of examples
libraries.paragraph: The Nexgen Rover is an educational robot suitable for Years 5-10. The library is a convenient way to get up and running quickly although strictly speaking it isn't absolutely needed. The rover uses Grove sensors and therefore one or two Grove libraries that are needed. It also uses Pololu light sensors and thus needs the QTRSensors library.

libraries.name: NEXNTC

CC310 hardware via Nordic CRYS when vendored; OnChip fallback otherwise. Requires ArduinoNRF (nrf52). See docs/VENDORING.md and docs/ONCHIP_BUILD.md.

libraries.name: NiusIMU

libraries.name: NiusThread
libraries.author: dunknowcoding (NiusRobotLab)

Form or join a Thread mesh with four calls (begin / setNetwork / start / process), then talk IPv6/UDP across it - or use the built-in CoAP layer (onCoapGet/onCoapPost/coapPost/coapGet) for resource-style control. The dataset and frame counters persist in flash, so nodes re-attach by themselves after a reboot. The complete official OpenThread C API stays available through Thread.instance(). Hardware-verified: two-node mesh (Leader + Child to Router), UDP multicast and CoAP LED control confirmed over the air, settings persistence across reset. Requires the ArduinoNRF board package.

Compatible with AVR, SAMD, ESP32, ESP8266, nRF52, STM32, RP2040 / RP2350, Renesas RA (UNO R4) and more.

libraries.name: NiusZigbee

Ships an SDCC CC2530 MAC/PHY helper firmware (raw 802.15.4 send/receive, hardware PAN/address filtering, Auto ACK, CCA transmit, retries, promiscuous sniffing) and a growing native Zigbee PRO stack on the nRF52840: short-address MAC + association join, active scan + parent selection, AODV route discovery and multi-hop forwarding, AES-CCM* NWK and APS security, end-to-end acked delivery, APS fragmentation, ZDO discovery and network management (Mgmt_Lqi/Rtg), source binding, network-state persistence, Trust-Center key-transport tooling (AES-MMO/HMAC specialized keys) with per-joiner install-code link keys and key rotation, broadcast transaction table, sleepy-end-device queue + keep-alive with the CC2530 v0.5 auto-ACK frame-pending bit, PAN-ID conflict + channel-change network manager, Touchlink + Green Power proxy/sink commissioning over real inter-PAN MAC frames, plus reusable ZCL device clusters and reporting helpers. Flash the module firmware with the ArduinoNRF board package's built-in CC-Debugger - no external TI programmer required. Extensible to more modules and a future Z-Stack backend.

Used in a sketch that only calls the library's `setup()` and `loop()` functions, it prints output like below for received signals and provides a command line interpreter to set radio type, GPIO-pins used, etc. Settings are stored in flash on the ESP32 using SPIFFS. OOKwiz tries to read the data from messages, example: `pulse(5906) + pwm(timing 190/575, 24 bits 0x1772A4)` (all time in µs).   • Cool game examplesand demos: minesRuner-Accel, minesRunner-gest, demos, testLayout, etc
  • Supports all possible led layouts.
  • Hot-swap the neopixel matrix by using rebuild()
  • Transformations such as rotate(), translate(), rotateMatrix(); Alongside with popMatrix() and pushMatrix().
  • Draw methods : setPixel(), line(), rect()
  • Display images using image()
And a lot more...

This library is part of the neopixel project an open hardware/software project to make easy create interactive games.

Find all .stl (3d) and gerber (PCB) files to build your own Pixel and Play console at Github Pixel and play Open Hardware.
Also a complete Assembly gide.

This project was born in 'Creative Electronics', a BEng Electronics Engineering 4th year module at the University of Málaga, School of Telecommunications.

Pixel Spork lets users code at their own comfort level by only requiring a few core tools to operate, but providing many more for power users. libraries.name: Portenta_H7_PWM
libraries.author: Khoi Hoang <khoih.prog@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: This library enables you to use Hardware Timers on an STM32H7-based Portenta_H7 board to create and output PWM to pins.
libraries.paragraph: These PWM channels, using Portenta_H7 Hardware Timers, still work even if other functions are blocking. Moreover, they are much more precise (certainly depending on clock frequency accuracy) than other software or ISR-based PWM, using millis(), micros() or Timer Interrupt. This important feature is absolutely necessary for mission-critical tasks. You can start, stop, change and restore the settings of any PWM channel on-the-fly.

libraries.name: Portenta_H7_Slow_PWM
libraries.author: Khoi Hoang <khoih.prog@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: This library enables you to use Hardware Timers on an STM32H7-based Portenta_H7 board to create and output PWM to pins.
libraries.paragraph: These PWM channels, using Portenta_H7 Hardware Timers, still work even if other functions are blocking. Moreover, they are much more precise (certainly depending on clock frequency accuracy) than other software PWM using millis() or micros(). That's mandatory if you need to use in applications requiring better accuracy. It now supports 16 ISR-based PWM-channels, while consuming only 1 Hardware Timer. PWM-channel interval can very long (ulong millisecs). The most important feature is they're ISR-based PWM-channels. Therefore, their executions are not blocked by bad-behaving functions or tasks. This important feature is absolutely necessary for mission-critical tasks. These hardware PWM channels, using interrupt, still work even if other functions are blocking. Max PWM frequency is limited at 1000Hz. Now you can change the PWM settings on-the-fly

libraries.name: Portenta_H7_TimerInterrupt

That's mandatory if you need to measure some data requiring better accuracy. It now supports 16 ISR-based Timers, while consuming only 1 Hardware Timer. Included data filters preprocess sensor data to filter noise and control varying intensities for example.

libraries.name: puara-module

This project is designed for artists and creators interested in developing distributed systems, creating interactive installations, building network-based projects.

libraries.name: Pubnub

It supports all Arduino Ethernet Client compatible hardware, including the Intel Galileo/Edison, ESP8266 and TI CC3000.

This was the only addition needed to make this library usable with protocols other than plain text in the will (eg. google protocol buffers).

libraries.name: PubSubClient3

libraries.name: PulsePosition
libraries.author: Paul Stoffregen
libraries.sentence: Send and receive multiple high resolution PPM encoded signal streams.
libraries.paragraph: Pulse Position Modulation (PPM) is a single-wire signal that encodes many Pulse Width Modulated (PWM) signals.  It's commonly used in radio control of hobby aircraft and drones, where a radio transmits the PPM signal, which is decoded into many PWM signals to control RC servo motors.  PulsePosition can simultaneously receive and send up to 8 PPM streams.

libraries.paragraph: PulseWetProbe is an Arduino library for MCU-only two-plate electrode sensing. It supports high/low pulsed drive, reversible two-plate role swapping, dry/wet and multi-point calibration, board-aware defaults, analogReadResolution-aware normalization, guarded ESP32 touch sensing when available, fixed-memory noise filtering, pro diagnostics, CSV output, optional JSON outside tiny mode, power-aware sampling, and anti-corrosion Hi-Z rest behavior. It does not claim certified EC, salinity, freezing-point, or RWIS accuracy.

libraries.name: PWFusion_TCA9548A
libraries.author: Playing With Fusion <TechnicalSupport@PlayingWithFusion.com>
libraries.sentence: TCA9548A I2C Multiplexer Library
libraries.paragraph: The TCA9548A allows up to eight I2C buses to be pragmatically connected to a micro-controller. Buses may be connected independently or multiple buses may be connected in parallel. This is a great way to read multiple sensors with the same I2C address from a single micro.

libraries.name: PWFusion_VL53L3C
libraries.author: Playing With Fusion <TechnicalSupport@PlayingWithFusion.com>
libraries.sentence: VL53L3C Time of Flight Sensor Library
libraries.paragraph: Arduino library built on top of the ST VL53L3C C API.  This time of flight (ToF) sensor improves on previous sensors from ST and is able to track up to four targets simultaneously. It utilizes an invisible class 1 laser to measure absolute distance regardless of the target color or reflectance. The maximum sample rate and ranging distance is dependent on ambient lighting conditions (1.4 meters in short mode, 3 meters in long mode).

libraries.name: PWM2motor_BNL

It is designed to be compatible with general-purpose motor drivers that typically use 10 pin headers (including power and ground). Ideal for compact robots and mobility projects.

libraries.name: PWMFreak
libraries.author: Colin MacKenzie
libraries.sentence: Configures the PWM frequency on a pin
libraries.paragraph: A very small library for configuring the PWM frequency for AVR based Arduinos. At least some of this code has been copied from the Internet, see PWMFreak.h for attribution.

libraries.name: PWMMotorControl
libraries.author: Armin Joachimsmeyer
libraries.sentence: Control brushed DC motors by PWM and uses optional attached encoders to drive fixed distances. For L298 or TB6612, or Adafruit Motor Shield
libraries.paragraph: With special CarPWMMotorControl for easy control of 2 or 4 motors of the obstacle avoiding arduino robot car kits. If slot-type photo interrupters or IMU / MPU6050 are attached to the encoder discs of such a kit, deterministic distances and turns can be driven. Examples include a follower car and an Bluetooth controlled obstacle avoiding car.

libraries.name: PWMOutESP32

SoftwareSerial, Adafruit_NeoPixel and DmxSimple are the most common cause of these problems.  PWMServo allows use of servo motors when these or other interrupt blocking libraries are required.

The basic capabilities include debug logging, software breakpoints, and inspection and modification of memory and GPIO state. On Cortex-M4-based architectures, this can also control hardware breakpoints and instruction stepping.

libraries.name: PyDuinoBridge

libraries.name: pyrpc
libraries.author: lu-maca
libraries.sentence: A simple RPC framework for exporting Arduino functions to a Python client

libraries.name: python esp bridge
libraries.author: Hamza Yesilmen <resmiyslmn@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Flash-once firmware that exposes every peripheral to Python over USB serial or Bluetooth.

One EspBridge.begin() call starts a FreeRTOS task model (separate TX, RX and network tasks) so blocking radio I/O never stalls peripheral traffic. Requires arduino-esp32 core 3.x. Also runs on the Nordic nRF52840 (Seeed XIAO / Adafruit Bluefruit core) with a capability-gated subset: BLE link, GPIO, ADC, PWM and I2C.

libraries.name: roo_scheduler
libraries.author: Dejwk <dejwk.oss@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Allows scheduling delayed and/or repetitive tasks.
libraries.paragraph: Works on boards that support C++ standard library (e.g. Espressif ESP32 family). Specifically, it requires the following standard headers: `<memory>`, `<queue>`, and `<functional>`. Uses `std::priority_queue` for storage, and therefore: (1) Maintains the queue in a flat vector, and thus, does not dynamically reallocate memory as long as the queue remains below its present capacity. (In most practical cases, the queue will stay within small bound capacity); (2) Scheduling a task, as well as looking up the nearest scheduled task, is O(log N), where N is the queue length, so it remains fast even in those rare cases when the queue gets longer. The tasks can be defined as function pointers, but also as inline lambdas, or generally as arbitrary callables, so it is convenient and idiomatic to make them stateful.

libraries.paragraph: This library allows to connect gamepad from Sega Mega Drive to Arduino and read buttons from it. No gamepad hardware modification needed.

libraries.name: segDisplay
libraries.author: Qmaker
libraries.sentence: A lightweight library for controlling 7-segment displays.
libraries.paragraph: It allows for easy control of common-cathode displays using native pin names, manual segment control, and direct functions for digits.

libraries.name: SegLCDLib
libraries.author: Petr Kracik
libraries.sentence: A library for LCD segment displays.
libraries.paragraph: Includes drivers for PCx85xx and similar segment display controllers. The library is designed to be easily extensible to support other controllers and LCD displays. Contains also mapping for LCD displays.

libraries.name: Segma
libraries.author: bboris
libraries.sentence: Dynamic indication with shift registers
libraries.paragraph: A simple way to control displays on seven/eight segment indicators with dynamic indication on shift registers

libraries.name: SegMap595
libraries.author: Dmitriy Efimov aka Erling Sigurdson <efimov-d-v@yandex.ru>
libraries.sentence: A single-class embedded-oriented Arduino-compatible C++ library for mapping the parallel outputs of a 74HC595 shift register IC to the segments of a 7-segment display.

libraries.name: Segment
libraries.author: Blake Tourneur <blaketourneur@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: The most powerful and popular available library for using 7/14/16 segment display, supporting daisy chaining so you can control mass amounts from your Arduino!
libraries.paragraph: This library is for using 7, 14 or 16 segment-displays wired to arduino parallel (each segment with a I/O pin) or with a shift register (data, clock, latch). Shift registers can be daisy-chained to control mass amounts displays off just a few pins. There is also support for common anode or cathode displays, and both displays with and without decimal points. Click the 'More Info' button below to visit the official Github Repo of this project, and view the full API/documentation.

libraries.name: semilimes
libraries.author: semilimes <https://www.semilimes.com>
libraries.sentence: sdk to allow MCUs to connect to semilimes
libraries.paragraph: The Semilimes SDK connects microcontrollers to the Semilimes server, enabling secure instant messaging with forms and widgets. It supports interaction in peer-to-peer chats, channels, and group chats, all while ensuring maximum cybersecurity through the Semilimes platform.

libraries.name: SemVerChecker
libraries.author: bkwoka
libraries.sentence: Lightweight Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0.0) parser and comparator for Arduino, ESP32, etc. Perfect for OTA updates and firmware compatibility checks.
libraries.paragraph: A highly efficient, zero-allocation library for parsing, validating, and comparing version strings (e.g. "1.0.0-beta"). Supports strict SemVer 2.0.0 rules and precedence comparison. Optimized for embedded devices like AVR, ESP8266, ESP32, etc.

libraries.name: SEN10724
libraries.author: alrevuelta
libraries.sentence: Provides functions to handle the SEN 10724 board.
libraries.paragraph: To be used with the SEN-10724 9 degrees of freedom sensor stick sold at Sparkfun, which contains three sensors (ADXL345 accelerometer, ITG-3200 gyroscope and HMC5883L magnetometer). Different functions are provided that allow to read data from the sensors, change its configuration parameters and calibrate them.

libraries.name: SendOnlySerial
libraries.author: Greg van Paassen <gregvanpaassen+github@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Lightweight serial output library that saves up to 175 bytes of RAM compared to Arduino's Serial
libraries.paragraph: Send-only alternative to Arduino's Serial library for ATmega328P boards. Supports all standard print functions, PROGMEM strings (but not String objects). Has a few debugging macros. Uses minimal RAM. For memory-constrained projects requiring serial debugging or logging.

libraries.name: SenseAir_S88_Async
libraries.author: Oleksandr Specled
libraries.sentence: Asynchronous, non-blocking Modbus library for SenseAir S8 CO2 sensors.
libraries.paragraph: Features a robust State Machine, CRC16 validation, ring buffer for command queuing, and self-healing mechanisms for lost connections. Designed for high-reliability systems and ESP32/ESP8266/Arduino architectures.

libraries.name: SenseBoxBLE
libraries.author: Felix Erdmann <f.erdmann@reedu.de>
libraries.sentence: Arduino library to send data over the senseBox BLE Bee
libraries.paragraph: This library allows you to send data over the senseBox BLE Bee. It is based on the phyphox_BLE library.

libraries.name: SensEdu
libraries.author: Vladyslav Sorokin, Azra Talić
libraries.sentence: API for SensEdu projects on the Arduino GIGA R1.
libraries.paragraph: Provides an interface to STM32H747 peripherals, such as ADCs, DAC, DMA, timers, and PWM, with extensive examples for each. The library uses direct register access to support low-level customization.

libraries.paragraph: There shouldn't be a reason to use it directly, but other libraries might depend on it.

libraries.name: Sensirion UPT Display

libraries.paragraph: The library provides functions to easily display sensor measurements and basic device information.

libraries.name: Sensirion UPT I2C Auto Detection
libraries.author: Jonas Stolle, Maximilian Paulsen
libraries.sentence: Automatically detects Sensirion Sensors on an I2C bus and reads out measurement data.
libraries.paragraph: Sensors can be read out collectively using a single method. The resulting data points include information about the sensor origin, units and the measurement timestamp.

libraries.name: Sensor

libraries.paragraph: This sensor wrapper makes retreiving mapped sensor values a breeze

libraries.paragraph: This library allow you to send filtered (mobile average) sensors data as a streeam of data in csv format.

libraries.name: SensorCurrent
libraries.author: Nicolas Fourgheon <boby15000@hotmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Mesure du courant alternatif (AC) avec les capteurs ACS712, SCT-013 et similaires : crête, RMS, puissance apparente.
libraries.paragraph: Permet de mesurer l'intensité crête, l'intensité efficace (RMS), la puissance apparente. Fournit une calibration automatique, un filtrage logiciel et une correction de facteur. Compatible avec les capteurs analogiques centrés sur Vcc/2.

libraries.name: SensorFusion
libraries.author: aster94
libraries.sentence: A library that makes using a IMU a breeze.
libraries.paragraph: Mahony and Madgwick algorithms.

libraries.name: SensorHub

libraries.sentence: Core communication and data processing hub for I2C-based sensors.
libraries.paragraph: SensorHub provides essential I2C read and write operations, multi-byte transactions, and connectivity verification for various sensors.

libraries.name: SensorLib

libraries.sentence: Commonly used I2C , SPI device multi-platform libraries

libraries.name: SensorManager
libraries.author: Si Carter <s1cart3r@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Modular sensor scheduling with non-blocking, time-based updates for Arduino projects.
libraries.paragraph: Lightweight C++ framework for managing multiple sensors in Arduino projects using non-blocking, time-aware scheduling. It enables each sensor to define its own update interval and initialization logic, promoting modularity and clean separation of concerns.

libraries.name: SensorModbusMaster
libraries.author: Sara Damiano <sdamiano@stroudcenter.org>
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for communicating via modbus with the Arduino acting as master
libraries.paragraph: This library is designed to use an Arduino as a modbus master to communicate with a sensor/slave via modbus RTU. It's specifically written with lots of "higher-level" functions to help out users who are largely unfamiliar with the modbus protocol and want an easy way to get information from a modbus device.

libraries.name: SensorNormalization
libraries.author: kalmak07
libraries.sentence: Library for line sensors.
libraries.paragraph: This library is designed to line sesor. Thanks to the mathematical function, the library effectively normalizes sensor readings from 0% to 100%.

libraries.name: SensorPlot WebInterface
libraries.author: Jason Rietzke
libraries.sentence: WebInterface to display Sensor-Data.
libraries.paragraph: This lib uses the ESP8266WebServer to create a WebInterface to display Sensor-Data you track.

libraries.name: SensorRoxoOBR

libraries.paragraph: Desenvolvida para simplificar a programação de robôs de linha da OBR. Esta biblioteca gerencia o sensor TCS34725 integrado a um multiplexador I2C, automatizando a troca de canais, normalização de dados e calibração para a identificação direta de cores essenciais como verde, vermelho, preto e branco.

libraries.name: SensorToButton
libraries.author: Nathan Ramanathan <nathan6ramanathan@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: An algorithm to convert analog Data into a Button.
libraries.paragraph: You can also use regular Buttons for this library. Main uses are a capacitive button, a HCSR-04 button, and etc

libraries.name: SensorWLED
libraries.author: Debinix Team <debinixteam@triatagroup.com>
libraries.sentence: Provides methods to retrieve instant and peak values from the ADC input. The Arduino library SensorWLED splits the input from a varying analog signal from the ADC into components, i.e., provides the capability of a sample-and-hold circuit.
libraries.paragraph: The library has methods that return ADC input as read i.e., instant, while other functions hold the peak sampled value while decaying with user-set decay parameters.

libraries.name: SensythingCore

libraries.sentence: Unified Arduino library for SensythingES3 family ESP32-S3 sensor boards
libraries.paragraph: Supports Sensything Cap and Sensything OX boards (FDC1004 capacitance and AFE4400 PPG/SpO2 sensors) with USB Serial, BLE, WiFi WebSocket, and SD card communication interfaces. Provides a consistent API across all boards with modular architecture for easy extension.
depends: ProtoCentral AFE4490 PPG and SpO2 boards library

libraries.name: Sequent Home Automation HAT

libraries.name: Serial Controlled Motor Driver
libraries.author: SparkFun Electronics <techsupport@sparkfun.com>
libraries.sentence: Use this to command the SCMD and connected chain.
libraries.paragraph: This library does the low level interface to the Serial Controlled Motor Driver.  It provides functions to control the driver, set motor drive level, inversion mode, and bridging mode.  It also includes a tool to randomly access control registers over serial, for debugging purposes.  This has been fully tested on the uno and Teensy 3.2.

libraries.name: Serial Data Exporter
libraries.author: Darash Desai <darash@lyvewave.com>
libraries.sentence: This library provides a simple way to collect and export data via Serial in various output formats.
libraries.paragraph: Currently supported formats include JSON output and output to the Arduino IDE Serial Plotter. Notably, JSON output using this library also enables simple data viewing using the Serial Data Viewer web tool: https://github.com/lyvewave/arduino-serial-data-viewer.

libraries.name: Serial_BLE

libraries.paragraph: Customizable Arduino and ESP32 BLE Serial library, compliant with Nordic UART Service and others. Supports both NimBLE and esp-idf BLE stacks.

libraries.name: Serial_Monitor

libraries.paragraph: (Crude) implementation of a transport protocol to allow two controllers to talk to each other via a serial (UART) interface without having to rely on timing or hardware flow control.

libraries.name: SerialBuffSender
libraries.author: Seifeddin Jenifen
libraries.sentence: sending buffer via serial
libraries.paragraph: The SerialSendBuffer Arduino library is a software library that provides a buffering mechanism for data and sending it via serial communication. The library allows Arduino programs to store data in a buffer and send it to a connected device over a serial communication channel.

libraries.name: SerialBus
libraries.author: Monteiro
libraries.sentence: Uses bit bagging to create async communication over a single wire as bus. Most ideal for sending short periodic signal messages.
libraries.paragraph: An Arduino library to create a simple serial-like communication that only needs one wire.

libraries.name: SerialCAN
libraries.author: Henrik Söderlund <henrik.a.soderlund@hotmail.com>
libraries.sentence: A library that lets you send data over Serial using the CAN communication protocol
libraries.paragraph: With supported end-to-end protection using crc8 to ensure the data integrity over high speeds. This library is compatible with the python-can library.

libraries.name: SerialCmd
libraries.author: Guglielmo Braguglia <guglielmo.braguglia@phoenixsea.ch>
libraries.sentence: Just another library to tokenize and parse commands.
libraries.paragraph: A Wiring/Arduino library to tokenize and parse commands received over a phisical/software serial port or buffer. From the original work of Stefan Rado & Steven Cogswell.

libraries.name: SerialCom
libraries.author: Willi Zschiebsch
libraries.sentence: Arduino Library for sending data
libraries.paragraph: With this library you can easily, send custom data packages from one arduino to another. The communication works in both directions and only needs two wires to archive this.

libraries.name: SerialCommand

libraries.paragraph: Arduino library for Serial Commands over a serial port

libraries.name: SerialCommand Advanced

libraries.sentence: A Wiring/Arduino library to tokenize and parse commands received over any serial port.
libraries.paragraph: Register commands, and start controlling your Arduino!

libraries.name: SerialCommandCoordinator
libraries.author: Matthew Miller
libraries.sentence: A memory-efficient, zero-heap, non-blocking serial command dispatcher.
libraries.paragraph: A lightweight string parser designed to safely map incoming serial commands to registered function addresses. It operates entirely without dynamic memory allocation (zero-heap) to prevent fragmentation. Features include automatic buffer overflow recovery, in-place parameter extraction, interactive sub-mode polling, and seamless compatibility across 8-bit and 32-bit Arduino architectures.

libraries.name: SerialCommandManager
libraries.author: Si Carter <s1cart3r@gmail.com>

libraries.name: SerialCommands

libraries.paragraph: Simple, small footprint, no dynamic memory allocation

libraries.name: SerialConfigCommand
libraries.author: cygig <rubbish52@hotmail.com>
libraries.sentence: SerialConfigCommand for Arduino allows user to set commands via the Serial Monitor easily.
libraries.paragraph: SerialConfigCommand can allow for commands with or without values to be set. Example: "LED=255", "Lock=1", "Start". The library checks the Serial buffer every x interval defined by the user, and parse the setting into commands and values.

libraries.name: SerialConsole

libraries.paragraph: Non-blocking serial command parsing with argument support, customizable configuration, and built-in help system. Works in Arduino IDE Serial Monitor or real terminals (PuTTY, VSCode). Optimized for low RAM usage on AVR boards.

libraries.name: SerialDebug

libraries.paragraph: Replacement to standard serial debug of Arduino

libraries.name: SerialDebugger

libraries.name: SerialDraw

libraries.name: serialEEPROM

libraries.paragraph: Supported/tested devices: AT24C128/256 and 24C01C

libraries.name: SerialFlash

libraries.paragraph: SerialFlash provides low-latency, high performance access to SPI Flash memory with a filesystem-like interface. Familiar file-based functions, similar to the SD library, are used to access data.

libraries.name: serialIO

libraries.name: serialMux

libraries.sentence: Serial multiplexer for Arduino
libraries.paragraph: This library provides a simple way to create multiple virtual serial devices that communicate over one physical serial connection. A virtual device can be used as a drop-in replacement for `Stream` like objects such as `Serial`.

libraries.name: SerialNetworkBridge
libraries.author: mobizt
libraries.sentence: Bridge TCP, UDP, and WebSocket client communication over serial.
libraries.paragraph: Enables non-networked Arduino boards to perform TCP, UDP, and WebSocket client operations. Bridges communication via a WiFi-capable host (ESP32/ESP8266) OR a PC/Raspberry Pi via USB (Python). Features include SSL/TLS support, datagram handling, and async events.

libraries.name: SerialRecord
libraries.author: Oliver Steele <steele@osteele.com>
libraries.sentence: Send and receive multiple values to and from the serial port, with error checking.
libraries.paragraph: This library is intended for novice programmers, as an alternative to Serial.print() and Serial.println() (for sending data on the serial port) and Serial.read() and parsing (for receiving data from the serial port). It is designed to be easy to use, to detect when it is used incorrectly, and to detect and report when it receives invalid data. Data is sent in a format that is compatible with the Serial Montior and Serial Plotter tools: comma-separated ASCII values, with optional field names. In conjunction with the "SerialRecord for Processing" library, it supports display of detected errors on the Arduino to the Processing log or canvas.

libraries.name: SerialRFID
libraries.author: Andres Garcia Mangas <agmangas@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Arduino library to read RFID tags from ID-innovations RFID readers (e.g. ID-12LA) using serial.
libraries.paragraph: Designed to be used with RFID readers connected to the SparkFun RFID USB Reader.

libraries.name: SerialRGBLed

libraries.name: SerialSDManager
libraries.author: Eric Thieme-Garmann

libraries.paragraph: SerialSDManager provides a simple command interface over the serial port to list, read, write, and delete files on a microSD card. It is used by the senseBox connect-app for remote file management and configuration.

libraries.name: SerialServo
libraries.author: Lilis

libraries.name: SerialTerminal

libraries.name: SerialTerminalIO

libraries.name: SerialToWifi

libraries.name: SerialTransfer

libraries.name: SerialTuning
libraries.author: TrebledJ <trebledjjj@gmail.com>

libraries.name: SerialUI
libraries.author: Pat Deegan
libraries.sentence: A user interface through the serial channel (menus, sub-menus and command execution), with support for navigation through the menu hierarchy and online help.
libraries.paragraph: With SerialUI, you can create a hierarchy of menus and submenus of arbitrary depth (limited only by ROM/RAM space). Each menu contains a list of menu items, which are either sub-menus (lead you to another level of menu items) or commands (actually perform some type of action). Exactly what happens when a user issues a command is determined by your callbacks.

libraries.name: SerialUtil
